text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:.
Business:
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Gold mines at Zlatna, Abrud and Baia de Aries are threatened with closure.
- Reforms in the in industrial sector will start with the restructuring of the public utilities.
- Fuel consumption across the country dropped by 15 percent following recent price hikes.
ADEVARUL
- The central bank postpones new method to compute reference exchange rates for the local leu currency.

- The gold and copper Mines in the western Carpathians reduced output following power cuts ordered by Renel RA electricity authority due to failure of the state-run mines to pay their electricity bills.
- Trade unions in petrochemical plans threatened to launch series of strike to protest against government plans to restructure the sector.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Prices for locally-made cigarettes expected to rise by 60 percent.
- Wirom SA of Germany plans to invest some $100 million to build gas storage tanks and pipelines in Romania.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Ex-president Ion Iliescu said the recent government decision to restore King Michael his Romanian citizenship was "unconstitutional".
- Bucharest police launches a joint project with city hall to gather the city's street children and beggars and offer them help.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Gypsy king Cioaba will be buried in Sibiu on Wednesday, the paper said.
- Romania's King Michael will meet President Emil Constantinescu, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and other politicians during his week-long visit to Romania, the paper says.
- Italian journalist Mino Damato claims he can prove that the Romanian HIV-infected children are the alleged victims of medical tests, the paper says.
- Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov has allegedly refused an invitation by his Romanian counterpart to meet in Bucharest, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica asked the Senate to lift parliamentary imunity for Senator Corneliu Vadim Tudor, of the Greater Romania Party.
- The Romanian-Hungarian partnership is on a good track, Foreign Minister Adrian Severin is quoted as saying.
ADEVARUL
- Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica threatened to sack Chief Prosecutor Nicoale Cochinescu over disagreements on reforms in the legal sector.
- Romania has not yet appointed an ambassador to NATO, the paper says.
- Stoica will ask prosecutors to probe into alleged irregularities related to adoptions of Romanian children by foreigners.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
